headline: The shorter boundary determines the next water column
statement: Unit-width bars have nonnegative heights. Return the total volume of water retained between them after rain.
intuition: Water above a bar is bounded by the smaller of the tallest wall to its left and right. Two pointers maintain these walls. Once the left maximum is no larger than the right maximum, the left column is settled regardless of anything farther inside.
approach: Start pointers at opposite ends and track left/right maxima.
Process the side with the smaller maximum, adding its maximum minus its bar height.
Move that pointer inward until all columns are settled.
correctness: For the processed smaller-maximum side, a wall at least that tall exists on the other side. Its limiting waterline is therefore known exactly. Each step adds the correct contribution for one unprocessed column and removes it. Summing these disjoint contributions gives the volume.
bruteForce: For each column scan both sides for their maxima, taking O(n²) time. Prefix/suffix arrays reduce time to O(n) with O(n) storage; two pointers retain only the needed boundaries.

complexity.explanation: Each pointer moves monotonically inward and each column is processed once.

pitfalls: Use the smaller boundary, not the taller one.
Update maxima before subtracting heights to avoid negative water.
